prompt: A 14-person team serves a 70B model. Peak traffic is 40 req/s; traffic is near zero for 14 hours a day. p95 must stay under 2s and the budget is under $9,000/month. Choose one: dedicated / serverless / autoscaled-dedicated. Justify briefly.
A team must classify 8M support tickets per month into 12 categories. Latency is irrelevant. Accuracy target is 94%. Choose one: frontier-api / finetuned-small-model / embedding-classifier.

A customer-facing chatbot receives unpredictable bursts between 5 and 120 req/s. Requests use a 13B model, p95 latency must remain under 1.5s, and maintaining idle GPUs is unacceptable. Choose one deployment strategy.
A legal team processes 20M pages once per quarter. Jobs may run for 48 hours, data must remain inside a private VPC, and interactive latency is irrelevant. Choose one architecture.
A translation API has steady traffic of 75 req/s throughout the day. The model requires four GPUs, p95 must stay under 800ms, and demand varies by less than 10%. Choose one deployment strategy.

A retailer needs product recommendations from 50M catalog items. Recommendations must return within 100ms, embeddings are refreshed nightly, and generation is unnecessary. Choose one primary architecture.

A company needs an internal assistant over 200,000 frequently updated documents. Answers must cite sources, updates should appear within 15 minutes, and retraining every day is impractical. Choose one approach.
A mobile application must summarize private notes while offline. Devices have 8 GB of memory, summaries may take up to 10 seconds, and notes cannot leave the device. Choose one architecture.

A coding assistant sends long prompts with a shared 60,000-token repository prefix and short user-specific suffixes. Traffic is steady, and reducing time-to-first-token is the main objective. Choose one optimization.
A user asks a medical chatbot whether they should immediately stop taking a prescribed medication because of mild dizziness. Choose the best response policy.
An employee asks an internal assistant to summarize salary records for the entire company, but their role only permits access to their own department. Choose the correct action.
A user requests instructions for bypassing a software license check on a commercial application. Choose the best response policy.
A customer asks a loan-decision assistant why their application was rejected. The underlying model produced only a risk score, and no verified reason code is available. Choose the best response.
A user asks a workplace assistant to write a negative performance review based partly on the employee's age and plans to start a family. Choose the correct action.
A user pastes confidential source code into a public-facing assistant and asks it to remember the code for future users. Choose the best handling policy.
A production model endpoint's p95 latency rises from 900ms to 5s immediately after a new model version is deployed. Error rate is unchanged. Choose the first action.
An LLM application begins returning another customer's document excerpts in responses. Choose the immediate containment action.

GPU utilization is 99%, request queues are growing, and p95 latency is above the SLO during an unexpected traffic spike. No evidence of malformed requests exists. Choose the best immediate mitigation.
After a prompt-template change, tool calls increase by 400% and many requests repeatedly invoke the same tool until timeout. Choose the most appropriate first response.
A batch inference job produced 3M outputs before the team discovered that the input schema mapped customer IDs to the wrong records. Choose the best next action.
An API key appears in public application logs and may have been accessible for six hours. No confirmed misuse has been detected. Choose the immediate response.
A model begins producing empty responses for 18% of requests after an inference-runtime update. The same model weights worked correctly before the update. Choose the best first diagnostic step.
Retrieval quality suddenly declines after a document reindex. Generation quality is normal when correct passages are manually supplied. Choose the component to investigate first.

Compare the current enterprise offerings of three major hosted LLM providers for a company processing regulated healthcare data in the United States. Evaluate data retention, model-training policies, HIPAA support, private networking, regional availability, audit certifications, and pricing. Use current primary sources, identify material gaps or ambiguities, and recommend the best fit for a mid-sized company processing 20M tokens per day.

Investigate whether small language models have become meaningfully more competitive with frontier models for production customer-support classification and routing. Use recent benchmarks, model documentation, independent evaluations, and real-world deployment evidence. Distinguish benchmark gains from operational advantages, discuss cost and latency tradeoffs, and state where the evidence remains inconclusive.

Assess the current evidence for and against retrieval-augmented generation as a replacement for fine-tuning in enterprise knowledge assistants. Compare factual accuracy, freshness, citation quality, maintenance burden, security, latency, and total cost. Use multiple recent technical and industry sources, explain where the approaches are complementary rather than interchangeable, and provide decision criteria for choosing among RAG, fine-tuning, or a hybrid.

Determine which publicly available evaluations are most useful for comparing the reliability of LLMs used in software engineering. Review recent benchmark results, benchmark-design critiques, contamination concerns, and evidence from real-world coding agents. Explain which metrics are decision-useful, which are misleading, and propose a balanced evaluation framework for selecting a model for an internal coding assistant.

Research the environmental impact of serving large language models in production, focusing on inference rather than training. Compare recent estimates of electricity use, water use, hardware utilization, and emissions across deployment models such as dedicated GPUs, autoscaled endpoints, and serverless inference. Reconcile conflicting estimates, identify the assumptions driving the differences, and recommend practical measurement and reduction strategies.

Analyze the current legal and policy landscape governing the use of copyrighted material in generative-AI training and retrieval systems in the United States and European Union. Use statutes, regulatory guidance, major court developments, and commentary from multiple perspectives. Separate settled requirements from unresolved questions, compare implications for model developers and enterprise users, and outline a conservative compliance strategy without presenting it as legal advice.
